validated_results.title: Micronutrients and the risk of renal cell cancer: a case-control study from Italy.
validated_results.reason: Hospital-based case-control study reporting a dietary vitamin B6 intake odds ratio for incident, histologically confirmed renal cell cancer.

extraction.comparison_type: Highest vs lowest quintile of intake
extraction.population: Hospital patients with incident histologically confirmed renal cell cancer and hospital controls with acute nonneoplastic conditions

sample_size.excerpt: Cases were 767 patients (494 men and 273 women) with incident, histologically confirmed RCC; controls were 1,534 subjects (988 men and 546 women) admitted to the same hospitals as cases for a wide spectrum of acute, nonneoplastic conditions.
sample_size.location: abstract; total_n derived from reported group counts 767 + 1534 = 2301

cases.excerpt: Cases were 767 patients (494 men and 273 women) with incident, histologically confirmed RCC; controls were 1,534 subjects (988 men and 546 women) admitted to the same hospitals as cases for a wide spectrum of acute, nonneoplastic conditions.

effect_size.excerpt: The ORs for the upper quintile of intake when compared with the lowest one were 0.80 (95% confidence interval, CI = 0.59-1.08) for retinol, 0.82 (95% CI = 0.61-1.10) for alpha-carotene, 0.90 (95% CI = 0.68-1.20) for beta-carotene, 0.94 (95% CI = 0.73-1.21) for beta-criptoxanthin, 0.85 (95% CI = 0.63-1.14) for lutein/zeaxanthin, 0.76 (95% CI = 0.57-1.01) for vitamin D, 0.75 (95% CI = 0.55-1.01) for thiamine, 0.88 (95% CI = 0.66-1.19) for riboflavin, 0.85 for vitamin B6 (95% CI = 0.64-1.13), 0.85 (95% CI = 0.64-1.12) for folate and 0.80 (95% CI = 0.60-1.07) for niacin. No meaningful associations emerged for lycopene (OR = 1.11).

confidence_interval.excerpt: The ORs for the upper quintile of intake when compared with the lowest one were 0.80 (95% confidence interval, CI = 0.59-1.08) for retinol, 0.82 (95% CI = 0.61-1.10) for alpha-carotene, 0.90 (95% CI = 0.68-1.20) for beta-carotene, 0.94 (95% CI = 0.73-1.21) for beta-criptoxanthin, 0.85 (95% CI = 0.63-1.14) for lutein/zeaxanthin, 0.76 (95% CI = 0.57-1.01) for vitamin D, 0.75 (95% CI = 0.55-1.01) for thiamine, 0.88 (95% CI = 0.66-1.19) for riboflavin, 0.85 for vitamin B6 (95% CI = 0.64-1.13), 0.85 (95% CI = 0.64-1.12) for folate and 0.80 (95% CI = 0.60-1.07) for niacin.
